commits.edited_message:
mprintf: avoid scanning strings twice for unbounded %s

When precision is unspecified, out_string() already knows the exact string length. Pass it directly to stream_run() instead of scanning again in stream_zrun().

Keep the bounded, NUL-aware scan for explicit precision, including non-NUL-terminated buffers. Document why the two paths differ.

Also trim the output-segment budget to 127 so it stays below the independent argument budget.

Closes #23019

-#define MAX_SEGMENTS   128 /* number of output segments */
+#define MAX_SEGMENTS   127 /* number of output segments */
 
 /* Lower-case digits. */
 const unsigned char Curl_ldigits[] = "0123456789abcdef";

commits.edited_message:
mprintf: make mprintf() and mfprintf() return -1 on error

Previously they returned the number of characters it output at the time of the error, but that is not only contrary to what POSIX does, it also makes it next to impossible for a caller to know when for example the output failed because out of disk space or similar.

Use the argument budget when accepting format conversions so the parser-side limits share one named bound.

Verified by test 2380
Closes #23112

coupling: The first commit reduces output storage to MAX_SEGMENTS == 127 while every parser check still uses the reduced macro, so that commit alone safely rejects the 128th segment. The second commit changes conversion acceptance to MAX_PARAMETERS == 128; on the original tree both macros are 128, so that commit alone is behavior-equivalent and safe. Together, output is a 127-element array while the conversion check permits ocount == 128, so the 128th conversion writes to output[127] and overflows formatf()'s stack buffer. Restoring either edited commit alone removes the fault: reverting the first restores 128 storage slots, while reverting the second makes the check use MAX_SEGMENTS again and reject the 128th conversion.
